title: Model routing
point: Send easy steps to a cheaper model and hard steps to a stronger one, and prove each route on a golden set by cost per completed task.
definition: Model routing assigns each step or request to a model by difficulty. A fixed router maps step types to models; a cascade tries a cheap model first and escalates to a stronger one when confidence is low.

objective.text: Given the step types in an agent loop and two model prices, design a fixed or cascading route, compute its expected cost, and name the golden-set measurement that approves it.

misconceptions.claim: The cheapest model that gives a plausible answer is always the cheapest choice.
misconceptions.correction: A cheaper call that fails more often triggers retries and re-runs. Judge a route by cost per completed task, which can rise even when the price per call falls.

misconceptions.claim: Routing is decided once, by intuition about which steps are easy.
misconceptions.correction: Measure quality per route on a golden set before and after any change. A step that looks easy, such as extracting dates from contracts, may fail badly on a smaller model.

l1: Most agent loops mix easy steps, such as classification, extraction and routing, with hard steps, such as planning and judgement. Easy steps rarely need the strongest model.
A fixed router sends each step type to a chosen model. A cascade tries a cheap model first and escalates to a stronger one when the cheap answer has low confidence.
Every route is proven on a golden set: a fixed list of real cases with known answers. Quality is measured per route, not only for the whole task.
l2: A task makes 10 calls. Six are classification or extraction and four need reasoning. On the strong model each call costs $0.02, so the task costs $0.20.
A cheaper model costs a fifth as much, $0.004 per call. Routing the six easy calls to it gives 6 times $0.004 plus 4 times $0.02, or $0.104 per task.
That is a 48 per cent saving per attempt. It counts only if the golden set shows the easy routes still succeed, because every failed extraction can force a re-run of the whole task.
l3: A cascade sends every call to the cheap model first. If 30 per cent are escalated to the strong model, the expected cost is $0.004 plus 0.3 times $0.02, or $0.010 per call.
That is half the strong-only price, but the confidence threshold sets the trade. Set it low and wrong answers slip through; set it high and most calls escalate, paying for both models.
Tune the threshold on the golden set and judge it by cost per completed task and task success together. Re-check after every model or prompt change, because confidence scores drift.
